title: Non-Fiction Text Features
keyIdea: Fact books have special parts that help you find things fast. The contents page is at the front: it lists the chapters in page order. The index is at the back: it lists words in ABC order with their page numbers. The glossary says what the special bold words mean. Headings tell you what each part is about. A fact book can be built as a list, in time order, or as questions and answers.

kid: A fact book tells you true things. You do not have to read it all. It has parts that help you find what you want.
The contents page is at the front. It lists the chapters and the page each one starts on. Want to read about what frogs eat? Find “What frogs eat … 10”. Then turn to page 10.
The index is at the back. It lists words in ABC order. Next to each word are the pages it is on. “pond 6, 7” means pages 6 and 7 tell you about ponds. The numbers are pages, not how many ponds.

Some special words are in bold. Bold means thick, dark letters. The glossary tells you what bold words mean. A heading at the top of a part tells you what it is about. Some pages are a list. Some go in time order: first, next, last. Some ask a question, then answer it.
adult: This lesson teaches children to find their way round an information book using its text features. It matches Common Core RI.1.5 and RI.2.5 (know and use text features such as headings, tables of contents, glossaries, bold print and indexes to locate key facts) and RI.3.5 (use text features and search tools efficiently). In England, Year 2 pupils are introduced to non-fiction books structured in different ways, and lower key stage 2 pupils retrieve and record information from non-fiction.

Key terms for ages 6 to 9: non-fiction, information text, text features, contents page (table of contents), chapter, page number, index, alphabetical (ABC) order, glossary, bold print, heading and subheading. Text structures at this age are list (facts in any order), chronological or time order (first, next, then, last) and question and answer.

Common mistakes: mixing up the contents page and the index, so a child hunts the contents for a single word. Reading the numbers in an index as chapters or as counts, rather than page numbers. Searching an index from the top instead of jumping to the right letter. And expecting the glossary to say where a word appears, or the index to say what it means.

In the lab your child uses one book, All About Frogs. They tap chapters on the contents page, look words up in the index and drop a new word into its ABC place, and drag bold words onto their glossary meanings. Then they sort questions to the right feature and name how three pages are built. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: Pick any fact book at home or at the library. Before reading, ask your child to find one thing using the contents page and one using the index. Say the page number out loud together, then check if you were right.

visual.caption: Which part of the book helps? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Find the chapter on frog homes

lab.caption: Flagship lab: use a frog book's contents page, index and glossary, sort questions to each, and name how pages are built.

practice.prompt: Where in a fact book is the contents page?
practice.hint: You look at it before you start, to choose a chapter.
practice.explain: The contents page is at the front. The index and the glossary are usually at the back.

practice.prompt: The contents page says chapter 2 starts on page {a} and chapter 3 starts on page {=a+k}. How many pages long is chapter 2?
practice.hint: Count on from page {a} to page {=a+k}.
practice.explain: From page {a} to page {=a+k} is {=k} pages, so chapter 2 is {=k} pages long.

practice.prompt: You want to know what “amphibian” means. Where do you look?
practice.hint: Which part tells you what special words mean?
practice.explain: The glossary tells you what special words mean. The contents page only lists chapters.

practice.prompt: You are on page {a}. The index says ponds are on page {=a+b}. How many pages forward do you turn?
practice.hint: Count on from page {a} to page {=a+b}.
practice.explain: From page {a} to page {=a+b} is {=b} pages forward.

pool.prompt: What does the index tell you?
choices: Which pages a word is on
pool.explain: The index lists words in ABC order with the pages they are on. The glossary says what words mean.

pool.prompt: The index says “tadpole 15, 16”. What does that mean?
choices: Pages 15 and 16 tell you about tadpoles
pool.hint: The numbers in an index are page numbers.
pool.explain: Pages 15 and 16 tell you about tadpoles. Index numbers are pages, not chapters or counts.

pool.prompt: Which word comes first in an index?
pool.hint: Look at the first letters: a, f, w. Which comes first in ABC order?
pool.explain: The index is in ABC order. a comes before f and w, so ant comes first.

pool.prompt: A word in a fact book is in bold. Why?
choices: It is a special word in the glossary
It is the name of the author
pool.hint: Where can you find out what a bold word means?
pool.explain: Bold words are special words. You can find what they mean in the glossary.

pool.prompt: A page says: “First, an egg. Next, a tadpole. Last, a frog.” How is it built?
pool.hint: First, next and last are time words.
pool.explain: The steps go in order with first, next and last, so it is time order.

pool.prompt: What does a heading tell you?
pool.hint: A heading sits at the top of a part.
pool.explain: A heading tells you what that part is about, so you can skip to the part you need.

pool.prompt: Chapter 4 starts on page {a}. It is {k} pages long. On what page does chapter 5 start?
pool.explain: Page {a} and {k} pages more is page {=a+k}, so chapter 5 starts on page {=a+k}.

pool.prompt: You want the chapter on what frogs eat. Which part helps you most?
pool.explain: The contents page lists the chapters and the page each starts on, so you can turn straight there.

pool.prompt: The index says “eggs {a}”. You are on page {=a+b}. How many pages back do you turn?
pool.hint: Count back from page {=a+b} to page {a}.
pool.explain: From page {=a+b} back to page {a} is {=b} pages back.
